instructions: * Heave: Frontal cone AoE. Tank to dodge as required.
* Feathercut: Frontal cleave tank-buster.
** Empowered Ketu: Adds a Bleeding debuff to the Tank. The second empower adds Vulnerability Up.

* Mindjack: Knocks players back and applies Out of Body. Each player must slowly return to their physical body in the middle of the arena, linked by a fiery line. Prototype Death Claws will spawn and slowly follow each player, stunning at melee range, while Prototype Bits spawn around the area and shoot line AoEs, also stunning on contact. Avoiding both should be prioritized over rushing, though taking too long will result in death. After a player recovers their body, they can proceed to attack the Death Claws.
Healers should prepare to heal through his occasional casts of Kenki Release, which hits the whole party.

Arbuda is a massive, four-armed, sword-wielding statue with powerful attacks. Non-tank players should stand at approximately 45 degrees off any of Arbuda's cardinal directions; if you consider his front heading to be 0 degrees, you want to be at 45, 135, 225. or 315. This ensures you'll have plenty of time to reposition to avoid two of Arbuda's main attacks.
*Fourfold Shear: is a slice on the tank, even if you move Arbuda follows you so buff up and get healed.

*Spirit Wave: Light raidwide that also spawns a persistent whirlwind on a random player - usually the ranged DPS or healer. After a short moment, it starts to repeatedly inflict damage and Vulnerability Up stacks on players still in it. Just move out and avoid the area.

*Touch of Slaughter: Targets a random player with a green marker, then leaps at them and sets their HP to a single digit number. The healer should heal them up ASAP, especially as this gets comboed with Hurricane Kick in the next phase, potentially killing the target.

*Spirit Wave: Light raidwide that also spawns a persistent whirlwind on a random player - usually the ranged DPS or healer. After a short moment, it starts to repeatedly inflict damage and Vulnerability Up stacks on players still in it. Just move out and avoid the area.
* Torpedo: Moderate tank damage.
Gold Lung no se limpia con Esuna; cada jugador debe usar una fruta.

instructions: Suggestion: Stack somewhere near the edge and let the tank draw the adds to one spot. AoE them down but keep an eye open for the boss's charge. Group up in the middle after the proximity AoE is done. Prepare for Patient Blade.
* Tsumuji-kaze: Uses Tornado. Damage is rather low. Adds seem to be melee in general.
** Odd pattern: Some adds target random players with line AoEs, while others damage the tank a few times.

* Allagan Gravity: Targets a random player with a large circle AoE that leaves behind a black puddle. Stepping in the puddle will cause it to detonate, dealing high damage and inflicting 40s of Heavy, after which it disperses. If the puddle gets detonated, the healer should help cleanse the debuffed player(s) so they can dodge upcoming mechanics.
* Aetheroplasm: AoE tankbuster. Avoid standing near the tank.
* Allagan Flare: Targets the tank with a proximity raidwide marker.
* Death Spin: Point-blank AoE hitting anyone in melee range - move away. Its animation is the boss raising its right claw and holding it high up in the air.

* Frost Breath: Two distinct attacks cast one after another. The first attack targets a non-tank and damages everything in a line from the boss to the targeted player. The second marks the tank and hits a wide arc in the tank's direction. Several ice puddles appear in the areas the attacks hit. The attack itself inflicts a dispellable frostbite Frostbite, while the puddles also inflict frostbite Frostbite for as long as a player stands in them.
* Earthquake: Melee-range area of effect followed immediately by a ring area of effect. Move to melee range or far range to dodge.

** After roughly 45 seconds, the Mud Slime will cast Corrupture, dealing damage to the entire party based on how large it became. If the Mud Slime was not allowed to grow at all, Corrupture instead only hits melee range. If the Mud Slime grows once, Corrupture will deal moderate party-wide damage. If the Mud Slime grows twice, it will explode immediately for very high damage while also inflicting a cleansable Damage Down.
* Royal Flush: Melee-range area of effect.
* Bog Bequest: Ring area of effect that leaves melee range safe. If Tokkapchi is on the edge of the arena, the opposite side is also a safe area.

* Commence Air Strike: Used by Julia. Eight Ceruleum tanks will drop from the sky, four on the outer edge, and four inside. Occasionally, Julia will use Roundhouse to knock the tanks around, with the added effect of dealing damage to and knocking back players in melee range. Regardless of if she uses Roundhouse or not, she will then follow up with Heirsbane targeting a tank to detonate it, dealing damage in a large area around the tank and causing all other tanks in the radius to also detonate.

* Commence Air Strike: Used by Julia. Eight Ceruleum tanks will drop from the sky, four on the outer edge, and four inside. Occasionally, Julia will use Roundhouse to knock the tanks around, with the added effect of dealing damage to and knocking back players in melee range. Regardless of if she uses Roundhouse or not, she will then follow up with Heirsbane targeting a tank to detonate it, dealing damage in a large area around the tank and causing all other tanks in the radius to also detonate.
* Stunning Sweep: Used by Annia. She jumps to a random player, then begins casting. Deals damage to players in melee range.
* Pendulum: Targeted proximity marker on the tank followed immediately by a proximity marker in the center of the arena.
* Chain Down: Targets a random non-tank player with a crosshair. Shortly after, that player will become Fettered, unable to act. Destroy the Iron Chain to free them.

* Coiling Ivy: Four Painted Ivy adds will appear at the feet of each player and inflict Fetter, thus rooting/binding them in place. The adds need to be targeted and destroyed to remove the debuff. The melee or short-range players can target their own add to break free, while ranged could help free other players from range, after freeing themselves.

* Hound out of Heaven: Proximity tether on a random non-Tank player. Eros charges at the targeted player for high damage. If the player was not far away enough to turn the tether purple, the attack also inflicts a stack of Vulnerability Up.
* Right Round: Untelegraphed melee-ranged AoE that deals minor damage and knocks players back.
* Venomous Breath: Cone AoE directed at tank that inflicts poison Poison.

* Meteor Rain: Targets the two DPS and the Healer with a large black circle AoE. When the AoE Markers disappear, they are replaced with a ground-targeted proximity AoE at the point each player was standing. This attack leaves behind boulders, which are necessary to evade other attacks.

* Deathly Ray (Masks): Faces appear on left or right side and cast lingering line AoEs directly across. The masks on one side will fire first, followed by the opposite side. There is no warning as to which side will fire first, so the healer must keep everyone's HP high enough to potentially survive the first hit.
* Augurium: Tankbuster. Hits in a cone-shaped area directly in front of the Alpha Zaghnal. This attack targets the ground, so the Tank can dodge it by stepping out of the way.
** Eventually, Mithridates will begin using all of its non tankbuster abilities simultaneously. When this happens, Allagan Thunder will only target the Tank and Healer.
** Eventually, Mithridates will begin using all of its non tankbuster abilities simultaneously. When this happens, Allagan Thunder will only target the Tank and Healer.
* Sap Shower: Circular attack targeting all non-Tank players.
* Clearout: Short cone attack from Unknown's front directed at the Tank.
* Setback: Short cone attack from Unknown's rear. Only used if a player is behind the Unknown and in melee range.
* 2,000-mina Swipe: Cone attack directly in front of the boss directed at the Tank.
* Eye of the Cyclone: Ring AoE with the only safe area in melee range of the boss.
:Hard Rock - tankbuster, healers prepare and tanks pop some cooldowns.
:Hard Rock - tankbuster, healers prepare and tanks pop some cooldowns.
:Smash-Crash - cleaving tankbuster that targets the tank with four tethers in a plus shape. The tethers cannot be intercepted, so everyone except the tank needs to stay away from the tethers.
:Tender Loin - room-wide AoE spell that does moderate damage. Healers be ready to AoE heal after it's cast
The boss will also use singular versions of these spells as heavy-hitting attacks on the tank.
* Dhrupad: Targets all non-tank players and inflicts them with a damage-over-time debuff. This will be used after every Transmute spell cast.
* Last Gasp: Tank Buster.
* Total Wreck: Tank Buster.
* Gnashing of Teeth: Tank Buster.
* Skull Dasher: Tank Buster
* Scratch: Tank Buster.
* True Tornado: Tank Buster. If cast with Double, drops a circular AoE under the tank's feet after the cast, which should be dodged.
* Aglaea Bite: Tank Buster.
* Anvil of Tartarus: Tank Buster.
* Dark Forte: Tank Buster.

* Curtain Call: During the long cast, two circular AoEs, similar to Eruption Forte will spawn in succession. Shiva will then spawn a huge ice crystal in the middle of the room (with a damage telegraph circle before it spawns; don't be near it) that the player must hide behind to avoid the attack. Any player not behind the ice crystal will be instantly killed. This bypasses tank invulnerabilities, so do not attempt to "cheese" this for uptime.

* Lifesbreath: The boss jumps to the edge of the arena, then shoots a line AoEs through the middle. After the line AoE, a line of butterflies will spawn in the same location, facing one half of the arena in alternating pairs. (⬆⬆⬇⬇⬆⬆⬇⬇ etc...) After a short delay, the butterflies will fire a line AoE (Lamellar Light) in the direction they are facing. Players must position themselves behind a butterfly to avoid the attack. Note that you can move through the line of butterflies before they fire. If hit by the butterflies players will receive doom Doom and must be healed up to full health to recover, or they will die. The second cast of this is accompanied by Loving Embrace, making one half of the arena unsafe to stand on. Loving Embrace fires off slightly after the butterflies' attack, allowing melee DPS to swap sides if necessary.

* Off My Lawn: Knockback usually combined with targeted AoE for each player, spread out to avoid overlapping. Every use after the first will be combined with Lines of Fire to make your positioning even more difficult to figure out; anti-knockback works fine if the proper safe lane is out of melee range or otherwise inconvenient.

* Explosives Distribution: Places two explosive tanks on the outside of the arena on conveyer belts. Arrows will soon appear indicating how far the explosives will move. One conveyor will have single arrows indicating the explosive will move to the half of the arena close to the boss, while the other conveyor will have multiple arrows indicating it will move to the half of the arena far from the boss. Move to a safe zone to avoid.

* Chemical Missile: All players but the tank are marked with point-blank AoEs, requiring them to spread out to avoid overlapping damage. Once they resolve, they will drop lava puddles that will debuff a player with Burning until they step out of them.
* Sonic Bloop: Moderate damage tank buster.
*Lightning Leap: Leaps in the opposite direction of the tank, releases a circular AoE and forms lightning lines on the floor that will explode.
*Ripper Claw: Moderate damage tank buster
*Blade: Telegraphed AoE tankbuster dealing high damage and inflicting windburn. Then spawns a telegraphed donut AoE (Wind Sickle) on the tank.
*Enduring Glory: Party-wide magical damage. Will wipe the party if the boss has too many Damage Up stacks. Can use a tank limit break to survive if he has more than 6 stacks.
*Quarantine: Telegraphed AoE tankbuster (Disinfection) and a stack marker on a random player. The tank should stay out while the other players stack together.
**For uptime, tanks may opt to remain in melee range and use an invulnerability cooldown, although it may not be possible to dodge the rotating AoEs that temporarily stun.

**Players on the JP data centers will tank the Bone Dragon on the center platform. This allows for an even spread of adds around the room, while minimizing confusion on where to pull the adds as 1 spawns per "path". This will also reduce damage taken by the DPS, as they will spend more time on the raised sections out of the poison.

**Players on the NA/EU data centers will tank the Bone Dragon on the far edge of the arena directly behind its spawn, as this will give DPS enough time to kill the Platinals even if they are racing towards the Bone Dragon due to being positioned incorrectly.

The raid will need to divide into their 3 groups based on their party (A, B, C): 1 for each path, which each has a platform. 4 people need to stand on each platform (preferably both healers, the tank, and one remaining DPS to kill adds) to light up the platform, which allows the other groups to kill their respective Atomos. Atomos does not need to be tanked but will continuously spawn adds (Valefors and Diras) that should be killed. Adds will always move to the pad unless otherwise aggroed, and healers on the platform can use AoE heals to produce threat if necessary, making it possible for all Atomos DPS to remain on Atomos. If non-platform DPS begin to aggro adds, instead of focusing Atomos, the tank will need to pick up adds aggro regardless of platform count. If a sector does not contain enough people to stand on the platform, once the room is sealed, several Iron Giants will spawn and quickly wipe the raid in order for the encounter to reset.
*Healers should be prepared to heal the party if/when the skeletons reach the dragon.

instructions: Thanatos is “ghostly” and cannot be harmed ordinarily. At the beginning of the fight, one of the Magic Pots will shoot green lines out to several alliance members, giving them a buff called File:Astral realignment icon1.png Astral Realignment. The first group to receive the buff is always A. File:Astral realignment icon1.png Astral Realignment allows you to deal damage to the boss. A tank with the buff should pick up the boss immediately, and a tank swap should occur whenever a tank picks up File:Astral realignment icon1.png Astral Realignment and the one on the boss loses it. Thanatos does have a cleave, so he should be faced away from the group and the pots.

Allagan Bomb initially does nothing. Each group takes one of the Vassagos with the large swords (A left, B north, C right - waymarks may sometimes be used to denote each party's add). Those Vassagos WILL NOT aggro anyone automatically, so each tank should stand in front of each adds to avoid the boss running to the middle. The boss will periodically spawn Allagan Balloon adds that need to be killed (high priority) before they reach the center, or they will explode and cause the Allagan Bomb to enlarge. If the bomb enlarges too much, it will explode and wipe the raid. In addition, an Allagan Napalm add may spawn and will have the highest priority to kill. The boss can be damaged once the 3 adds are down.
*Non-tanks should not be directly in front of a Vassago, because they will periodically used untelegraphed frontal cleaves.
*If you have File:Astral realignment icon1.png Astral Realignment and are ghostly, DPS the boss. If not, kill adds. Healers should keep the pots alive.
